rows.notes: Museum page lists 'die Landekapsel der Sojus-Mission TM-19' as an original; en.wikipedia Soyuz TM-19 says Energia gave it to Speyer in 2010, permanent display.

rows.item: Soyuz 29 descent module (used by Sigmund Jaehn to return from Salyut 6, 1978)
rows.notes: Only Wikipedia (de: Sojus 29 and the museum article) says it has been in the Libeskind wing since 2011; museum site fetched but gave no object page. Soyuz 29 is a 7K-T ferry, Orrery has no 7K-T entry; soyuz-t is the nearest ref, mapping is the operator's call.

Collection record says authentic J-2, 'On Display' in the Space Gallery, but gives no serial and does not say whether it flew; kind is a guess (flown / unflown / test unknown). Museum asks visitors to confirm it is on show.

rows.item: Goddard rocket engine (1929), lent by NASM
rows.notes: 1929 engine, not the 1926 rocket; record does not say if flown. Search listing says Energy Hall, object page gives no display status.

Wikipedia (Project Gemini) lists TTV-2 at Museum of Scotland; Commons category is filed as a Gemini boilerplate in the National Museum of Scotland but is also cross-filed under National Space Centre Leicester. NMS site returned 403, so current display not confirmed.
Commons photo (2012) only; museum page says 'numerous spacesuits' without naming this one. Not known whether flown.
